question: A randomised controlled trial with 50,000 participants reports a statistically significant reduction in systolic blood pressure of 1 mmHg with a new drug (p = 0.001). This result is definitely clinically meaningful.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Large sample sizes can make tiny differences statistically significant. The p-value here (0.001) is driven by the sample size of 50,000, not by a large effect. Critical appraisal distinguishes statistical significance from clinical relevance — a 1 mmHg BP reduction is below any threshold of practical importance.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Statistical significance depends on sample size — with 50,000 participants, trivially small differences become statistically significant. A 1 mmHg reduction has no established clinical benefit. Clinical significance requires assessment of effect size and real-world impact, not just p-values.
